title: Tory Bruno Named Honorary Chair Of World Space Week 2027
summary: Tory Bruno, President of National Security at Blue Origin, has been named Honorary Chair of World Space Week 2027. This appointment highlights his significant contributions to the space industry.

title: New Novaspace forecast: 6,500+ EO satellites to launch by 2035
summary: Novaspace predicts over 6,500 Earth observation satellites will launch by 2035, generating $155.9 billion in manufacturing revenue due to increased government demand for sovereign intelligence and surveillance capabilities.

title: Elve qualifies millimeter-wave amplifiers for spaceflight
summary: Elve, a California startup, has qualified its 100-watt millimeter-wave Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier platform for spaceflight. The qualification was supported by U.S. Space Force Small Business Innovation Research funding.

title: What’s next for ISR in space
summary: A SpaceNews panel discusses the future of Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) in space, featuring insights from experts recorded in May.

title: Moog Highlights Huntsville Expansion and New Hardware-in-the-Loop Lab During Space and Missile Defense Symposium
summary: Moog Inc. announced a major expansion of its Huntsville facility, including a new secure Hypersonic/Interceptor Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) lab. The announcement was made during the Space and Missile Defense Symposium.

title: Rock West Composites® Is Premiering Its New STRATOPultrusion™ Product Line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference
summary: Rock West Composites is unveiling its new space-grade STRATOPultrusion™ product line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference in August. The event will take place in Salt Lake City, Utah.

title: LatConnect 60 selects Transcelestial’s Space Optical Network for SWIRSAT imaging constellation
summary: LatConnect 60 has partnered with Transcelestial to use its Space Optical Network for the SWIRSAT-1 mission, enabling optical communications for the imaging constellation. This collaboration highlights advancements in space-based data transmission technology.

title: Draper Selects Proteus Space for Advanced On-Orbit Mission
summary: Draper Laboratory has selected Proteus Space to support an advanced on-orbit mission. Proteus Space, a dual-use aerospace company, will provide rapid, end-to-end access to space for the mission.

title: Moog Inc. Expands METEORITE Satellite Bus Capacity for High-Maneuverability Missions
summary: Moog Inc. has expanded the capacity of its METEORITE satellite bus to support high-maneuverability missions. This development enhances the company's offerings in satellite technology.

title: Eoptic, Inc. Selected to Supply DeepScan™ Imaging Payloads Scheduled for Launch in 2027
summary: Eoptic, Inc. has been chosen to provide DeepScan™ imaging payloads for a mission launching in 2027. The company specializes in advanced multi-spectral and multi-modal imaging systems.

title: The earliest galaxy 'swallowed' by the cannibal Milky Way left a scar at its heart
summary: The Milky Way galaxy consumed an earlier galaxy, leaving a scar at its core. This marks the earliest known instance of galactic cannibalism in our galaxy's history.

title: Nancy Grace Roman Telescope live updates: NASA readies Roman for launch
summary: NASA is preparing the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope for launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket. The mission aims to explore the universe once deployed.

title: It's been 20 years since Pluto lost planet status. Will it ever get its title back?
summary: Pluto's reclassification as a dwarf planet 20 years ago remains controversial, with an astronomer arguing the decision was a mistake.

title: New 'Star Trek' documentary featuring William Shatner hits theaters this fall, celebrating 60 years of Trek
summary: A new documentary titled 'Star Trek' featuring William Shatner will be released in theaters this fall, celebrating 60 years of the franchise. The film is described as a tribute to 'Star Trek'.

title: How a huge fleet of 17 spacecraft discovered something surprising about solar eruptions
summary: A fleet of 17 spacecraft measured a solar eruption from multiple vantage points, revealing its full extent. This discovery highlights the importance of distributed space missions in understanding solar phenomena.

title: Bad weather delays launch of China's historic Chang'e 7 mission to moon's south pole
summary: Bad weather has delayed China's Chang'e 7 mission to the moon's south pole. The new launch date has not been announced.

title: Launching 10,000 tiny 'femtosats' to Saturn? NASA funds 18 futuristic spaceflight ideas
summary: NASA has selected 18 futuristic spaceflight concepts for its Innovative Advanced Concepts awards, including a proposal to launch 10,000 tiny 'femtosats' to Saturn. The awards aim to support cutting-edge research and transform unconventional ideas into viable technologies.

title: How will NASA's astronaut training hub change with commercial space stations?
summary: NASA's astronaut training hub at Johnson Space Center is evolving to adapt to the rise of commercial space stations, reflecting growing collaboration between NASA and private industry in human spaceflight. A recent tour highlighted these changes and the future of space exploration.

title: 'We Want to Believe' book explores the reality of UFOs: 'It's always going to be more likely that someone is wrong about what they saw' (interview)
summary: The book 'We Want to Believe' by Adam Kirsch examines humanity's fascination with UFOs, suggesting that misinterpretations are more likely than extraterrestrial encounters. The interview highlights the cultural and psychological aspects of UFO sightings.

title: What Lake Bonneville Left Behind
summary: The drying of Lake Bonneville left behind playas that became sites for technological innovation and exploration. These areas witnessed both engineering feats and dramatic stories of survival.

title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 4982–4987: Back to Our Regularly Scheduled Programming
summary: The Curiosity Mars rover resumed its planned operations after a brief detour to study an erosional surface. It is now back on track to continue its ascent up Mount Sharp.

title: APOD: 2026 August 22 – Mostly Perseids
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) for August 22, 2026, features an image related to the Perseids meteor shower. The APOD is a daily astronomy image with an explanation by a professional astronomer.

title: NASA Shares Views of August Solar Eclipse from Ground, Air, Space
summary: NASA captured views of the August solar eclipse from various locations including ground, air, and space. The eclipse, which passed over Greenland, Iceland, and Spain, revealed the Sun's corona to observers in the path of totality.

title: TB 26-04 Updates and Modernization of NASA’s Chemical Equilibrium with Applications (CEA) Code
summary: NASA has updated and modernized its Chemical Equilibrium with Applications (CEA) code, a key tool for propulsion system analysis. The update enhances equilibrium chemistry, rocket performance, and shock calculations used by NASA and the aerospace community.

title: Webb Opens Treasure Chest
summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope captured an infrared image of the 'Treasure Chest,' a cometary globule within the Carina Nebula's star-forming region. This feature, known as the Cosmic Cliffs, highlights an isolated cloud of gas and dust with a dense core.

title: NASA’s Artemis II Crew Set to Receive Congressional Space Medal of Honor
summary: NASA's Artemis II crew will receive the Congressional Space Medal of Honor from President Trump during a ceremony at Johnson Space Center. The four astronauts, including three from NASA and one from CSA, are being honored for their upcoming lunar mission.

title: SmallSat 2026
summary: NASA will host storytelling sessions by experts at the SmallSat 2026 event in the Exhibit Hall, featuring presentations on small satellites, technology, and missions.

title: Artemis Mission Patches
summary: NASA conducted a terminal countdown simulation for the Artemis III mission at Kennedy Space Center, featuring mission patches from Artemis I and II. The event took place inside the Rocco A. Petrone Launch Control Center.

title: NASA’s Roman telescope nears launch, reaches final integration and rehearsal milestones
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is nearing its launch, scheduled for August 30, after reaching final integration and rehearsal milestones.

title: LandSpace’s Zhuque-3 topples following milestone landing
summary: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 rocket toppled after achieving a milestone landing, marking a significant step for Chinese commercial rocketry.

title: Ship 41 Completes Engine Testing Ahead of Flight 14
summary: Ship 41 has completed engine testing in preparation for Flight 14. Ship 40 is being transported back to Starbase from Christmas Island.

title: Stoke Space conducts second stage fit checks, completes first stage engines ahead of Nova debut
summary: Stoke Space has completed fit checks for its second stage and finished building the first stage engines for its Nova rocket, aiming for a debut launch around 2026. This progress comes as the company competes in the reusable launch vehicle sector alongside high-profile projects like SpaceX's Starship.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: Zhuque-3, a methalox rocket developed by LandSpace, successfully completed its second flight and achieved a first-stage landing. This milestone marks progress in reusable rocket technology for the company.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has delivered Starship Ship 40 to Christmas Island, with plans to return it to Starbase for further testing and preparation. This marks another step in SpaceX's ongoing development of the Starship program.

title: Launch Preview: Chang’e 7 headlines week of Chinese and Starlink launches
summary: China is preparing for the Chang'e 7 lunar mission following a recent launch failure. The mission will be part of a busy week of launches alongside Starlink missions.

title: Firefly promote next block of Alpha amid Eclipse progress
summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing the development of its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also making progress on its Eclipse program. The company is promoting its upcoming Alpha rocket block as it continues to progress in these areas.

title: Blue Origin overviews plan for dual pad ops at Cape Canaveral
summary: Blue Origin is planning dual launch pad operations at Cape Canaveral as it restores its primary launch pad at LC-36A. The company shared details about its expansion plans for increased launch capabilities.

title: Rocket Lab advances via series of announcements
summary: Rocket Lab has established a new subsidiary in Germany and introduced a containerized mobile launch system. These moves represent strategic expansion and innovation in the company's launch capabilities.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of the agency's contributions to space exploration and technology.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft designed for microgravity experiments and safe Earth return.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission aims to study the Sun's corona using this technique.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 is set to experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's precise orbital alignment.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipses and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona, which is otherwise difficult to study due to the rarity and brevity of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This presents a unique opportunity for testing and innovation in a deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A drone test flight at ESA's ESTEC facility in the Netherlands demonstrated a student-developed radar retroreflector technology. This marks the first flight of a payload designed for future sounding rocket missions.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to observe the Sun's corona by blocking out the Sun's disk, simulating an eclipse. The mission involves two satellites playing a game of hide and seek to achieve this.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with Europe's space industry on September 16-17 at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands.

title: Letara Raises ¥2.6B to Build its Hybrid Rocket Engine Tech
summary: Japanese propulsion startup Letara raised ¥2.6 billion ($16 million) in a pre-Series A funding round to develop its low-cost hybrid rocket engine technology.

title: SpaceWERX Announces 2026 STRATFI Awardees
summary: SpaceWERX announced the 2026 STRATFI awardees during the Fed Supernova conference. The Space Force revealed the new recipients of the Strategic Funding Increase program.

title: Op-ed: The Technologies That Could Define the Future of Space
summary: Daniel Biedermann, a partner at NewSpace Capital, discusses the key technologies shaping the future of space. The op-ed highlights emerging innovations in the space industry.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C
summary: Muon Space secured $250 million in a Series C funding round to expand its satellite production capacity and support a wider range of missions.

title: Portal Books Dedicated Falcon 9 Amid Constrained Launch Market
summary: Portal Books a dedicated Falcon 9 launch while collaborating with Maverick Space Systems to sell remaining fairing space for rideshare opportunities in a constrained launch market.

title: SpaceX’s Mobile Ambitions: Build, Partner, or Buy?
summary: SpaceX is exploring strategies to compete with major telecom providers like AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon by expanding into mobile services. The company aims to leverage its satellite and launch capabilities to tap into a lucrative revenue opportunity.

title: White House Publishes S&T Strategy for National Security
summary: The White House released its National Security Science & Technology Strategy through the Office of Science and Technology Policy. This strategy aims to guide national security efforts through scientific and technological advancements.

title: Zeno Power Books its First Nuclear Mission to the Moon
summary: Zeno Power has secured its first commercial payload agreement with Firefly Aerospace to send a nuclear-powered heating unit to the Moon by 2028. The mission, part of Firefly's CS-8 CLPS mission, will demonstrate Zeno's capability to provide 5W of power for lunar operations.

title: Deep Dive: FY27 Defense Space Budget
summary: The U.S. Space Force's FY27 budget request has been highlighted as a record-breaking $71.3 billion. This budget request has drawn significant attention in the space industry.

title: Slingshot’s Portal Adds New AI-Powered Missions
summary: Slingshot Aerospace enhanced its Portal platform with AI-powered capabilities to improve monitoring of the increasingly crowded space environment. The update aims to assist operators in tracking and managing space assets more effectively.

title: Fireside Chat with German Space Command: Featuring Major General Michael Traut
summary: Major General Michael Traut, Commander of the German Space Command, leads Germany's military space operations to protect assets and integrate space capabilities. The discussion highlights Germany's focus on space defense and allied coordination.

title: White House Targets Support for 1,000 Launches Per Year by 2030
summary: The White House announced a goal to support over 1,000 space launches and reentries annually by 2030 through a new National Security Presidential Memorandum. This initiative aims to boost U.S. space industry capabilities and national security.

title: The Evolution of the Space Edge With Voyager CTO Paul Tilghman
summary: The article discusses the evolution of spaceborne computing, focusing on the shift towards the 'space edge' rather than just orbital data centers. It features insights from Voyager's CTO, Paul Tilghman.

title: Starcloud Adds $250M to Series A at a $2.3B Valuation
summary: Orbital data center startup Starcloud raised an additional $250 million for its Series A round, increasing its valuation to $2.3 billion just five months after the initial raise. The funding was led by Manhattan West.

title: Space Norway Appoints Rune Jensen as Acting CEO With Morten Tengs Departure
summary: Space Norway has appointed Rune Jensen as acting CEO following Morten Tengs' departure from the role at the end of August. The company will now search for a permanent CEO.

title: Sypris Electronics Wins Manufacturing Deal to Support LEO Constellation
summary: Sypris Electronics secured a manufacturing contract to produce power processing units for an unnamed next-generation Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellation. The deal highlights Sypris Electronics' expanding role in supporting advanced satellite infrastructure.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C to Build Large-Scale Constellations
summary: Muon Space secured $250 million in a Series C funding round to expand its large-scale satellite constellations and enhance mission capabilities. This investment marks a significant milestone in the company's growth trajectory.

title: Phantom Space Names Worth Wray as COO
summary: Phantom Space has appointed Worth Wray as its chief operating officer to oversee day-to-day operations and business scaling. The company aims to enhance operational efficiency and capital formation as it grows.

title: Rocket Lab Launches SAR Satellite for Japan’s iQPS
summary: Rocket Lab launched a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite for Japan's iQPS on August 21 from New Zealand. This marks Rocket Lab's ninth launch for the Japanese company.

title: Rocket Lab’s Bold Move to Acquire Iridium: Analysts Break Down the Strategy
summary: Rocket Lab announced plans to acquire Iridium, marking a significant move in the satellite sector. Analysts are dissecting the strategic implications of this acquisition expected to reshape the industry.
